name: risk_parity_signal_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Risk parity allocates capital inversely proportional to volatility so that each position contributes equal risk. Applied intraday across a basket of 5-10 stocks, this approach generates a directional signal when the risk-parity weighted basket diverges from NIFTY 50. If the equal-risk basket underperforms NIFTY by > 15 bps, it suggests temporary mispricing in the basket constituents. The inefficiency arises because risk parity is used for portfolio construction (Bridgewater, etc.) but rarely as a signal generator. By comparing the risk-parity portfolio's return to the benchmark, we identify when lower-risk names are disproportionately sold (opportunity to buy) or bought (opportunity to sell).
universe: NIFTY 50 constituents — select top 10 by inverse-ATR weighting
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹100 Cr; ATR(14) / close must be > 0.003 to ensure minimum tradability

indicators.name: ATR_14
indicators.params: ATR(high, low, close, 14) for each constituent

indicators.name: RP_Weight
indicators.params: (1 / ATR_14_i) / sum(1 / ATR_14_j for j in basket)

indicators.name: RP_Return_30
indicators.params: sum(RP_Weight_i * ROC(close_i, 30)) for i in basket

conditions: RP_Spread < -15 bps (risk-parity basket underperforming NIFTY — low-risk names oversold)
long.confirmation: RP_Spread stops declining (RP_Spread > RP_Spread[1 bar ago])

conditions: RP_Spread > 15 bps (risk-parity basket outperforming NIFTY — low-risk names overbought)
short.confirmation: RP_Spread stops rising (RP_Spread < RP_Spread[1 bar ago])

entry.entry_price: market order on the most dislocated constituent in the basket (largest individual deviation from its VWAP)

exit.target: RP_Spread reverts to 0 (basket re-aligns with NIFTY)
exit.stop_loss: RP_Spread widens to -30 bps (for longs) — 2x entry threshold
exit.signal_exit: RP_Spread crosses zero from entry side

risk.position_sizing: Inverse-ATR weighted: higher allocation to lower-vol names

filters.vix_filter: India VIX between 12-22 for longs; VIX > 14 for shorts
filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:30 (ATR warm-up) or after 15:10
filters.volume_filter: All basket constituents must have traded > 1000 shares in last 10 bars
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY 50 intraday range < 2% (avoid extreme trend days where RP spreads are driven by macro, not mispricing)
filters.spread_filter: All basket constituents: bid-ask spread < 5 bps
filters.event_filter: Remove any constituent with earnings today; replace with next eligible by inverse-ATR weight
other_filters: Minimum basket size of 7 stocks after filters

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — risk parity as a signal is uncommon; the spread computation requires simultaneous tracking of 10 stocks, adding complexity that deters simpler competitors

weaknesses: The strategy trades only the single most dislocated stock, not the basket — this concentrates idiosyncratic risk and the individual stock may diverge from the basket signal
Risk parity weights depend on ATR(14) which is unstable on 1-min bars; small changes in ATR can cause large weight shifts, creating spurious RP_Spread signals
During genuine risk-off events (credit crisis, geopolitical shock), the RP_Spread dislocation is fundamental, not temporary — mean-reversion assumption fails
prior_art: Bridgewater All Weather risk parity; Qian (2005) 'Risk Parity Portfolios'; Maillard et al. (2010) on equal risk contribution; application as signal generator rather than portfolio construction is novel
notes: Could be extended to trade the full basket (multiple legs) for true risk parity, but this increases complexity and brokerage costs significantly. Single-stock entry keeps costs manageable.
